cell.label: Patient presents with signs and symptoms consistent with parkinsonism. Idiopathic Parkinson's disease confirmed based on clinical exam?
Consider immediate-release carbidopa/L-dopa (Sinemet) or a dopamine agonist.
Consider referral for apomorphine (Apokyn) therapy. If no improvement, refer for possible neurosurgery.
If severe dyskinesia, reduce carbidopa/levodopa (L-dopa) dose; if patient is taking controlled-release preparation, change to immediate-release; consider amantadine (Symmetrel).
If no improvement, refer for possible neurosurgery.

If motor complications, fractionate carbidopa/L-dopa therapy five times, a day, and consider adding a dopamine agonist, MAO-B inhibitor, or COMT inhibitor. If severe, consider referral for apomorphine (Apokyn) therapy.
If disease progresses, increase immediate-release carbidopa/L-dopa dose or increase dopamine agonist to the maximum tolerated dose and then add carbidopa/levodopa.
Consider CT or MRI to rule out normal pressure hydrocephalus or a vascular cause; consider referral to a subspecialist.

footnotes.footnote: Abbreviations: COMT, catechol O-methyltransferase; MAO-B, monoamine oxidase-B.
From Rao SS, Hofmann LA, Shakil A. Parkinson's disease: diagnosis and treatment. Am Fam Physician 2006;15(74):2046-2054.
